spots.name: National University of San Marcos
spots.summary: The National University of San Marcos is a public research university located in Lima, the capital of Peru. In the Americas, it is the first officially established and the oldest continuously operating university.

spots.name: Government Palace

hours.note: Closed Fri, Sat, Sun

spots.summary: The Government Palace, also known as the House of Pizarro, is the seat of the executive branch of the Peruvian government, and the official residence of the president of Peru. The palace is a stately government building, occupying the northern side of the Plaza Mayor in Peru's capital city, Lima.

spots.name: Cathedral of Lima

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Cathedral Basilica of Lima, commonly known as the Metropolitan Cathedral of Lima, is a Roman Catholic cathedral in Lima, Peru. It is the seat of the Archdiocese of Lima. Its construction began in 1535 by Francisco Pizarro and was completed in 1797, having been built in its present form between 1602 and 1797.

spots.name: Plaza Mayor, Lima
spots.summary: The Plaza Mayor, also known as the Plaza de Armas, is the main public square of the historic centre of the city of Lima, Peru. It dates back to the foundation of the city by Francisco Pizarro on 18 January 1535.

spots.name: Archbishop's Palace, Lima

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: The Archbishop’s Palace of Lima, the capital of Peru, is the residence of the Archbishop of Lima, and the administrative headquarters of the Archdiocese of Lima. It is located at the Plaza Mayor, in the Historic Centre of Lima.

spots.name: Larco Museum
spots.summary: The Larco Museum is a privately owned museum of pre-Columbian art, located in the Pueblo Libre district of Lima, Peru. The museum is housed in an 18th-century vice-royal building. It showcases chronological galleries that provide a thorough overview of 5,000 years of Peruvian pre-Columbian history.

spots.name: Monastery of San Francisco
spots.summary: The Basilica and Convent of San Francisco is a Catholic church building located in the Historic Centre of Lima, Peru.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Basilica and Convent of San Francisco, Lima

spots.name: Basilica and Convent of Santo Domingo
spots.summary: The Basilica and Convent of Our Lady of the Rosary, commonly known as the Convent of Santo Domingo, is a Catholic religious complex located in the city of Lima, Peru.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Basilica and Convent of Santo Domingo, Lima

spots.name: Plaza San Martín
spots.summary: San Martín Square is one of the most representative public spaces of the city of Lima, Peru. It is located at the ninth block of Colmena avenue, within the Historic Centre of Lima which was declared a World Heritage Site in 1988 by UNESCO.

spots.name: Basilica of Nuestra Señora de la Merced

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Basilica and Priory of Nuestra Señora de la Merced is a Roman Catholic church located in Lima, Peru. It was designed in the Baroque style known as Churrigueresque. The church was built under the supervision of Friar Miguel de Orenes in 1535.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Basilica and Convent of Nuestra Señora de la Merced

spots.name: Palacio de Torre Tagle

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Palacio de Torre Tagle is a residential mansion built during the colonial era of Peru that currently houses offices of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Peru. It is located in the Jirón Ucayali in the historic centre of Lima, two blocks southeast of the Plaza Mayor.

spots.name: St. Peter's Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Basilica and Convent of Saint Peter, formerly known as Basilica of Saint Paul after the school of the same name, is a Catholic church located in the historic centre of Lima, Peru.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Basilica and Convent of San Pedro, Lima

spots.name: Q677387

hours.note: Closed Tue

spots.summary: Huaca Pucllana, or Huaca Juliana, is a great adobe and clay pyramid located in the Miraflores district of central Lima, Peru, built from seven staggered platforms.

spots.name: Presbítero Matias Maestro
spots.summary: Presbyter Matías Maestro Cemetery, formerly the General Cemetery of Lima, is a cemetery, museum and historical monument located in the Barrios Altos neighbourhood of Lima District, in Lima, Peru. Inaugurated on May 31, 1808, it was the first pantheon in the city since burials were previously held in the city's churches.

spots.name: Historic Centre of Lima
spots.summary: The Historic Centre of Lima is the historic city centre of the city of Lima, the capital of Peru.

spots.name: Lima Art Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Lima Art Museum is an art museum in Lima, Peru. The museum is located in the Palacio de la Exposición. The museum was inaugurated in 1961. The collection includes ceramics, textiles, sculptures, and paintings spanning almost 3,000 years of history, from the pre-Columbian to Contemporary periods.

spots.name: Catacombs of Lima

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Catacombs of Lima are underground ossuaries in the historic centre of Lima, Peru. The catacombs were built under the Basilica and Convent of San Francisco and currently function as a museum.

spots.name: Parque de la Exposición
spots.summary: The Park of the Exhibition, known between 1999 and 2004 as the Grand Park of Lima, is a park located in the neighbourhood of Santa Beatriz, itself part of the buffer zone of the historic centre of Lima, Peru.

photo.author: No machine-readable author provided. Sancebau assumed (based on copyright claims

spots.name: Sanctuary of Saint Rose of Lima
spots.summary: The Sanctuary of Saint Rose of Lima, also known as Santa Rosa de los Padres, is a sanctuary dedicated to Saint Rose of Lima. It is located in the remains of Oliva's house, including the well used by the family, which serves as a highlight of the convent among visitors.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Sanctuary of Saint Rose of Lima

spots.name: Simón Bolívar
spots.summary: Simon Bolivar, also known as General Bolivar, is a bronze equestrian statue of Simón Bolívar by Adamo Tadolini. There are three casts. The original is located in the Plaza Bolívar in Lima, the first copy is in the Plaza Bolívar in Caracas and the second copy is in United Nations Plaza in San Francisco, California.

spots.name: Plaza Dos de Mayo
spots.summary: The Dos de Mayo Square, known as the Óvalo de la Reina until 1866, is a public square located in Lima, Peru. Located on the southwestern edge of the historic centre's bufferzone, it serves as the junction of several important avenues, including Alfonso Ugarte, La Colmena and Colonial avenues.

spots.name: Place of Memory, Tolerance and Social Inclusion

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Place of Memory, Tolerance and Social Inclusion is a museum in Lima, Peru, dedicated to the Peruvian internal conflict of the 1980s and 1990s. It opened in 2015 and is managed by the Ministry of Culture.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Place of Memory, Tolerance and Social Inclusion

spots.name: Lima Civic Center
spots.summary: The Lima Civic Center is an architectural complex located next to the Paseo de los Héroes Navales in the district of Lima, on the land previously occupied by the Lima Penitentiary. It was projected with the intention of becoming a civic-urban landmark for the city, housing State offices, a hotel and a convention center.

spots.name: Equestrian statue of Francisco Pizarro
spots.summary: The Equestrian statue of Francisco Pizarro is a series of three bronze equestrian statues of Spanish Conquistador Francisco Pizarro by U.S. sculptor Charles Cary Rumsey. The statues are located in Buffalo, Trujillo and Lima. The latter two cities are Pizarro's places of birth and death, respectively.

spots.name: Sanctuary of Las Nazarenas

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Sanctuary and Monastery of Las Nazarenas is a church in Lima and is the site of the Peruvian Catholic procession of the Lord of Miracles, Señor de los Milagros, who is also the patron of the city. It was constructed together with the Monastery of Nazarenas, after a major earthquake it was finally completed in 1771.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Sanctuary and Monastery of Las Nazarenas

spots.name: El Campo de Marte
spots.summary: The Campo de Marte, also known as the Plaza de la Revolución, is a public park in Jesús María District, Lima, Peru. It is one of the largest parks in the metropolitan area of the city, and similar in size to the Park of the Exhibition and the Park of the Reserve.

spots.name: Palacio Municipal de Lima

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: The Municipal Palace of Lima is a government building located on the third block of Union Street, next to the Plaza Mayor, in the Historic Centre of Lima, Peru. It functions as the seat of the Metropolitan Municipality of Lima.

photo.author: No machine-readable author provided. Manuel González Olaechea assumed (based on

spots.name: Jirón de la Unión
spots.summary: Union Street is a major pedestrian street in the Damero de Pizarro, an area of the historic centre of Lima, Peru. The street starts at the Puente de Piedra, and continues until it reaches Paseo de la República Avenue. The road continues on the northern side of the Rímac River as Trujillo Street.

spots.name: Iglesia del Sagrario

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of the Sanctuary is a Catholic church in Lima, Peru. It is located on the second block of the Jirón Carabaya, between the Archbishop's Palace and the Cathedral, and facing the main square of the city.

spots.name: National Museum of Archaeology, Anthropology and History of Peru

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The National Museum of Archaeology, Anthropology, and History of Peru is the largest and oldest museum in Peru, housed at the Palacio de la Magdalena, located in the main square of Pueblo Libre, a district of Lima, Peru.
spots.wikipediaTitle: National Museum of Archaeology, Anthropology and History of Peru

spots.name: Parque de la Reserva

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Parque de la Reserva is a park located in downtown Lima, in Peru. Built in an irregular shape, it is located between two of the city's principal streets, the Paseo de la República expressway and Arequipa Avenue.

spots.name: Legislative Palace
spots.summary: The Legislative Palace is a government building that serves as the seat of the Congress of Peru, the legislative branch of the Peruvian government. Located at Ayacucho street, it lies next to next to the Bolivar Square and forms part of the neighbourhood of Barrios Altos, itself part of the historic centre of Lima.

photo.author: Congreso de la República del Perú from Lima, Perú

spots.name: Casa de Aliaga
spots.summary: The Casa de Aliaga is a colonial-style building located in the historic centre of Lima, Peru. It was built on a huaca, dating back to May 1536, at the beginning of the founding of the city, and belonged to Conquistador Geronimo de Aliaga.

spots.name: Casa O'Higgins
spots.summary: The Casa O'Higgins is a colonial-style building located in the historic centre of Lima, specifically located in the Jirón de la Unión, a few metres from the Plaza de Armas of the Peruvian capital.

spots.name: Church of San Agustín, Lima

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Basilica and Convent of San Agustín is a Catholic temple located at the junction of the fourth block of Jirón Camaná with the second block of Jirón Ica, a few blocks from the main square of the city of Lima, forming part of its historic centre.

spots.name: Museum of Natural History, Lima
spots.summary: The Natural History Museum in Lima, is Peru's most important museum of natural history. It was established in 1918 and belongs to the National University of San Marcos.

spots.name: El Olivar, Peru
spots.summary: Bosque el Olivar is a public park located in the neighbourhood of the same name in San Isidro District, Lima, Peru. Named after the olive trees located there since their introduction in 1560, it is part of the cultural heritage of Peru.

spots.name: Museum of Italian Art

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: The Museum of Italian Art is a public museum in Lima, Peru. It is the only European arts museum in Lima. Openened in 1923, it is now managed by the Peruvian Ministry of Culture.

spots.name: Panteón de los Próceres
spots.summary: The Panteón de los Próceres is a crypt inside the old Church of San Carlos, located at the former Real Convictorio de San Carlos in the historic centre of Lima, that holds the remains of 24 of the national heroes of the Peruvian War of Independence.

spots.name: Miraflores Central Park
spots.summary: Miraflores Central Park, commonly known as Kennedy Park, is a public park located in Miraflores, Lima, Peru. The park serves the district's main square, and is divided into two areas, one of which gives the park its common name.

spots.name: Edificio Rímac

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Rímac Building, also known as the Roosevelt House, is a building located in the centre of the city of Lima, Peru. It is currently under the administration of the insurance company Rímac Seguros. It is located at 101/157 Roosevelt Avenue and 1177/1199 Jirón de la Unión.

spots.name: Iglesia de la Recoleta

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of the Sacred Hearts of Jesus and Mary, also known as the Iglesia de la Recoleta, is a Catholic church in the Plaza Francia in the historic centre of Lima, Peru. It was declared Cultural heritage of Peru in 2001.

spots.name: Plaza Bolívar
spots.summary: Bolívar Square, also known as Congress Square or Inquisition Square, is a public square located at the second block of Abancay Avenue, in the neighbourhood of Barrios Altos in Lima, Peru. It is three blocks east of the city's main square and forms part of the city's historic centre.

photo.author: No machine-readable author provided. Manuel González Olaechea assumed (based on

spots.name: Casa de Correos y Telégrafos

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Casa de Correos y Telégrafos is the central post office of the city of Lima, Peru. The building is located at Conde de Superunda street in the historic centre of Lima, near the Plaza Mayor. The building was constructed in 1897 in the Beaux-Arts architectural style.

spots.name: Pasaje Olaya
spots.summary: Pasaje José Olaya is a pedestrian alleyway located in the Damero de Pizarro, next to the Plaza Mayor of Lima, Peru. It is the location of a statue of the same name, which was declared part of the Cultural heritage of Peru alongside the other statues located within the historic centre of Lima in 2018.

spots.name: Casa de Osambela
spots.summary: The Casa de Osambela, also known as the Casa de Oquendo, is a building built during the colonial era of Peru. It stands on the site of the old novitiate of the Dominican fathers, destroyed by the earthquake of 1746, and part of the garden, facing the Calle de la Veracruz in the historic center of the city of Lima.

spots.name: Plaza Bolognesi
spots.summary: The Plaza Bolognesi is a roundabout located in the Lima District and the Breña District, in the capital of Peru. It is located at the intersection of Brazil Avenue, Arica Avenue, Alfonso Ugarte Avenue, Guzmán Blanco Avenue, and 9 December Avenue.

spots.name: Teatro Segura
spots.summary: The Teatro Manuel Ascencio Segura is a theatre and concert hall located in the Jirón Huancavelica of Lima, Peru. First built in 1615, it is considered the oldest theatre in Latin America.

spots.name: National Library of Peru

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: The National Library of Peru is the national library of Peru, located in Lima. It is the country's oldest and most important library. Like the majority of Peruvian libraries, it is a non-circulating library. It has two branches: the old building is on Abancay Avenue and the modern building is on Avenida Javier Prado.

spots.name: Love Park, Lima
spots.summary: Alberto Andrade Carmona Park, better known as Love Park, is a public park in Lima, Peru.

spots.name: Casa Fernandini, Lima
spots.summary: The Casa Fernandini is a historic residence located in the historic centre of Lima, Peru. It was built in 1913 and is located at 400 Jirón Ica. It was designed by Claude Sahut in an eclectic style.

spots.name: Teatro Municipal
spots.summary: The Municipal Theatre of Lima, inaugurated as the Teatro Forero, is a theatre and concert hall in the historic centre of Lima, Peru. It is home to the country's National Symphony Orchestra.

spots.name: Residencial San Felipe
spots.summary: The Residencial San Felipe is a residential complex for middle-class families located in Jesús María District, Lima, Peru. It is built in the former premises of San Felipe racetrack, with its construction being decided in 1962 by the military government of Ricardo Pérez Godoy.

spots.name: Plaza Francia
spots.summary: The Plaza de Francia, also known by its former name, Plazoleta de la Recoleta, is a public square in the historic centre of Lima, Peru.

spots.name: The Eye that Cries
spots.summary: The Eye that Cries is a memorial that was born as a private initiative designed to honor the thousands of victims of the internal conflict in Peru, to strengthen the collective memory of all Peruvians and to promote peace and reconciliation in the country.

spots.name: San Cristóbal Hill, Lima
spots.summary: San Cristóbal Hill is a hill in Lima, Peru. It overlooks the city's districts of Rímac and San Juan de Lurigancho, and forms part of the Andean Mountain Range. Once considered an Apu by the pre-Columbian cultures that originally inhabited the area, it was given its current name by Francisco Pizarro in 1535.

spots.name: Lamp of the Three Graces
spots.summary: The Lamp of the Three Graces is a sculpted lamppost next to San Martín Square, in the historic centre of Lima, Peru. It is based on a marble work of Germain Pilon, a French Renaissance sculptor, where the Three Graces are holding the heart of Henry II of France.

spots.name: University City of the National University of San Marcos
spots.summary: The University City of the National University of San Marcos, generally known as the University City of Lima or simply University City, is the main campus of the National University of San Marcos and is located in Lima District.
spots.wikipediaTitle: University City of the National University of San Marcos

spots.name: Avenida Nicolás de Piérola
spots.summary: Nicolás de Pierola Avenue, also known as La Colmena Avenue, is a major avenue in the Historic Centre of Lima, Peru. It functions as the southern limit of the historic quarter's Damero de Pizarro. It starts at Dos de Mayo Square, continuing for seventeen blocks until it reaches Miguel Grau Avenue.

spots.name: Paseo Colón
spots.summary: 9 December Avenue, also known as Paseo Colón, is an avenue in the Historic Centre of Lima, Peru. The street is named after the statue of Christopher Columbus, one of thirteen statues located along its four blocks.

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Museo Amano

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Showcases Peruvian textiles.

spots.name: Luis Miro Quesada Garland Hall

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: One of the most popular art galleries in Lima. The exhibition rooms are spacious, and the exhibitions themselves are generally very good. Work on show is mainly by local artists, with the occasional foreign contribution. Artists who display their work here usually go on to acquire a good reputation in the national art scene.
